steps: Pull software in Scout if the ticket needs it, and cold start if required.

Inspect and clean the sensors. Check each camera feed in Scout, then clean any dirty sensor within reach. Use the elevated platform for the center pod if the site has one; if not, don't climb for it. Dirt or smudges on a lens will fail DTV.
If it's raining, turn on sensor cleaning in Scout's Cleaning System section (Air Only, Short duration).
In the expanded Mission panel, swap the stack mode to CALIBRATION. This starts a log.
Stage the truck at the start of the DTV corridor, lined up with the ground markings.
Make sure no other truck is collecting in the corridor.
In Scout's side panel, scroll to Calibration Verification and tap the ▾ arrow to open it (see picture). Check it shows Ready.
Pick Drive Thru Verification in the procedure dropdown.
Press Start, wait about 5 seconds, then drive the corridor at about 5 to 10 mph.
Stop completely at the end, wait 5 seconds, and press Stop.
Wait for the result. PASS or FAIL comes back within about 5 minutes.
dtv_run.caution: Manual driving only. The left seat operator stays in the truck for the whole run.
dtv_run.source: Standard Dev Ops Test Procedures (Nov 13, 2026), Drive Thru Verification; Drive-Thru Calibration Verification design doc; Terminals SOP 4.1 (Inspect & Clean AV Sensors); DTV Data Collection working doc (sensor cleaning, rain); Calibration Runbook (cleaning kit in precipitation)
